paragraphs: Here's what Paul teaches me in this last stretch of his letter, friend. Contentment is not about how full your cupboard is. He says, "I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances," and he says it from chains (Philippians 4:11, 1:13). He knew "being filled and being hungry," "having plenty and having need," and the secret was the same in every one of them (Philippians 4:12).

So what is the secret? It's "I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength" (Philippians 4:13). I think that line gets put on a lot of T-shirts as if it means "I can do anything I want." In this letter, I believe it means Christ gives Paul strength to stay content in the plenty AND in the hunger. Same Christ, every kitchen, full or empty.

And look at what God does with a gift. Paul calls what the Philippians sent "a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God" (Philippians 4:18). Then he says, "my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus" (Philippians 4:19). So, baker, whatever you have to give today, give it to God's people with an open hand. He sees it, He is pleased with it, and He is the One who takes care of what you need.
